answer: Recursive zero-knowledge reputation commitments bind each agent’s accumulated stake to a succinct proof chain, while verifiable delay primitives impose a sequential cost that any cloned identity must repay from genesis; like a jetty resisting a forged echo, the ledger rejects replay without fresh state. An information-theoretic reduction then shows that spoofing requires inverting the delay’s crystal-hard transcript under uniformly sampled challenges, so adversarial advantage decays with each recursive layer.
